info.name: Sentinel
info.summary: Watches the things Nextcloud's own defences do not watch, and tells you when they change
Veghează asupra lucrurilor pe care apărarea proprie a Nextcloud nu le urmărește, și te anunță când se schimbă
info.description:
Nextcloud defends itself well. It throttles password guessing, hashes passwords properly, sets the right headers, offers two-factor authentication, and checks that its own files have not been altered. Sentinel does not repeat any of that.
What it does is answer the questions nobody asks until it is too late. Who has two-factor authentication and who does not. Which application passwords were last used in February and are still valid. Whether a file in the installation changed, and whether that change was expected. What the web server hands out to anyone who simply asks for it. And when any of it changes, who is told.
It has no opinion about how you share. A public link without a password is the feature working as intended, and a page that complains about it every week is a page nobody reads. What is watched is how a link is used compared with how that same link is normally used.
* **A posture page** that checks what core does not, with the reason and the fix beside each finding * **A file baseline you can acknowledge**, so a deliberate patch stops raising an alarm and a real change is the only thing that does * **A self-probe** that asks this server, as an anonymous visitor, for the files that must never be served — the configuration, the log, the .git directory an app left in the web root * **A watch for files changing very fast**, which is what ransomware on somebody's laptop looks like from the server's side, with the option of disabling the account outright * **Watchers** for an account becoming an administrator, two-factor being switched off, an app being enabled, a trusted domain changing, or a link being opened by a crowd it was never sent to * **An inventory** of public links, sessions and application passwords, with how each is being used and a way to end it * Every finding explains what it means and what happens if it is ignored, because a warning nobody understands is a warning nobody acts on
Sentinel changes nothing on its own unless you ask it to. It reports, and it acts only when told.
info.author: Cristian Casapu
